contents_summary: XLSX (Table_1.xlsx), one sheet read in full: per-patient table of the 29 cohort patients (rows numbered 1 to 29) with surgical, facial nerve, tumor and functional-outcome columns plus an abbreviations footnote. Row owners are not identified in the article text, so all extracted facts are unresolved and review_only.

sheet_reviews.contents: Sheet1 read in full: a header row, 29 numbered per-patient rows (rows 2 to 30) with sex, age, initial and revision surgery data, facial neurorrhaphy, radiosurgery, NF2, House-Brackmann and Modified Rankin grades, tumor side, location, size and volume, approach, outcome, follow-up and complications, and an abbreviations footnote in row 34.

blocks.contents: Header row with 24 column titles; two adjacent columns share the title "Facial neurorrhaphy".
blocks.clinical_relevance_notes: Column titles only; not a clinical measurement.

blocks.contents: Twenty-nine per-patient data rows numbered 1 to 29; every cell read and transcribed.
blocks.clinical_relevance_notes: Per-patient surgical, facial nerve and functional data for the 29 cohort patients.
limitations: Row owner not identified in the article text; numeric row labels are not linked to any roster patient and no attribute-matching is used.

blocks.contents: Abbreviations footnote in row 34 (rows 31 to 33 are empty).

limitations: Formulas not evaluated; stored cell values read. The volume column prints long decimal values and one scientific-notation value, kept as printed.

Rows are numbered 1 to 29 and are not linked in the article text to the three illustrative cases or to any roster patient; every fact is unresolved and review_only. Attribute similarity to an illustrative case is not used as ownership.
Two adjacent columns are both headed "Facial neurorrhaphy"; their distinction is not defined, so facts from them are marked uncertain.
Cell values are cohort supplement data and may differ from the article tables or text; no reconciliation was attempted.
No embedded images; formulas not evaluated.

transcriptions.text: Abbreviations: ; FN – facial nerve; HB – House–Brackmann grade; HHFN – hemihypoglossal-facial neurorrhaphy; I-surgery – initial surgery; MFA – middle fossa approach; mRS – Modified Rankin Scale; N/A – not available; NF2 – neurofibromatosis type 2; R-surgery – revision surgery; RSA – retrosigmoid approach; rVS – recurrent or remnant vestibular schwannoma; SRS – stereotactic radiosurgery; TLA – translabyrinthine approach
